structured_output.summary: Phase 92 is a careful, well-evidenced documentation/tooling follow-up. The 23-command gate in docs/checks/phase-92.json actually executed, all commands exited 0, and its source_sha256 (3e64b178…) equals the reviewed fingerprint, so this is executed evidence rather than prose. The central new control, scripts/check-published-payload.py, is genuinely fail-closed: it compared 129 published files (all of crates/scm-sdk/src and examples, Cargo.toml.orig, README, LICENSE, NOTICE) byte-for-byte against the retained crates.io receipt for 0.1.1, rejects added/changed/symlinked/duplicate/traversal paths, and has real negative tests (tools/test_g10_release.py:37). Its deliberate gap (normalized Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/.cargo_vcs_info.json) is covered by tools/live_evidence.py runtime_fingerprint, which binds root Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE, NOTICE and the whole src/examples tree and is also in the gate. All seven phase-91 findings have concrete, checkable dispositions: CHANGELOG.md:3-15 now carries the real archive SHA-256, source commit and the packaged example bullet, and tools/test_ci.py:242 asserts those values against the receipt; the version-independent documentation assertions now run before the version guard with a working negative test (tools/test_ci.py:211); tools/response_defaults.py:37 binds each of the three additive Rust APIs to its declaration and to the packaged example with six drift mutations; docs/VALIDATION.md:38-42 records the unmeasured 27,216-case typed corpus explicitly; the committed-range whitespace check is in the gate. No SDK runtime input changed and the tag/registry artifact were not touched. Two things keep this below the threshold. First, the newly CI-gated command set starts with `git diff --check 840c090..HEAD`, but .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml checks out with actions/checkout defaults (no fetch-depth), so the base commit will not exist in the shallow clone and the contracts-and-package job should fail at its first gate command; the phase's own stated deliverable is that CI runs this focused gate, and no remote run of this workflow exists yet to disprove it. Second, "actual CI observations" are retained only in docs/checks/release-ci-0.1.1-observation-01.json, which shows the 0.1.1 runs as waiting/running (nonterminal) and is referenced by nothing — not docs/phase-status.json, the plan, docs/CI.md or docs/RELEASE.md — while docs/RELEASE.md:107 tells readers current remote qualification is recorded in phase status, where only the phase-8 run 13 appears.

findings.description: The contracts-and-package job now runs `python3 tools/check_phase.py --phase 92 --verification-only` (ci.yml:72), and commands_for(92) begins with `git diff --check 840c090..HEAD` (tools/check_phase.py:73). The checkout step sets only `persist-credentials: false`; `fetch-depth` is not set anywhere in the repository, so actions/checkout v4 performs its default depth-1 clone and commit 840c090 is not present. `git diff --check 840c090..HEAD` then exits nonzero, check_phase.py breaks on the first failing command (tools/check_phase.py:327-334) and the whole focused gate fails remotely. Phase 91's CI-executed gate contained no commit-range command, so this is newly introduced here, and the only retained remote observation (docs/checks/release-ci-0.1.1-observation-01.json) is for commit 7efd137 under the previous workflow, so no run of this configuration exists. I could not execute git or trigger CI, so this is a static determination from the workflow and the default action behaviour.
findings.required_fix: Set `fetch-depth: 0` on the contracts-and-package checkout step (or make the committed-range whitespace check skip/deepen when the base commit is unreachable), and add a tools/test_ci.py assertion that whenever commands_for(the CI-executed phase) contains a commit-range git command the workflow checkout requests full history. Re-run the gate remotely and retain the result before advancing.

findings.description: Plan item 92.1 requires retaining "actual CI observations". docs/checks/release-ci-0.1.1-observation-01.json exists and is honest (runs 16/17 at 7efd137 are "running" and "waiting", with the limitation "waiting/running is not a passing CI result"), but nothing references it: the phase-92 scope_evidence block, the phase-91 delivery block, docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md, docs/CI.md and CHANGELOG.md contain no pointer, and the phase-92 record states no remote CI status at all. Meanwhile docs/RELEASE.md:107 says "Current remote qualification is recorded in phase status", where the only remote_ci entries are phase 8's run 13 (docs/phase-status.json:574, 641-650), and docs/CI.md:108-115 still narrates run 12. A reader therefore cannot find the actual, nonterminal CI state of the published 0.1.1 source from the ledger that claims to hold it.
findings.required_fix: Add an explicit remote CI record for 0.1.1 to the phase-92 (or phase-91 delivery) entry in docs/phase-status.json citing docs/checks/release-ci-0.1.1-observation-01.json and stating plainly that the runs were nonterminal at observation time, and update the docs/CI.md run narrative and/or docs/RELEASE.md:107 pointer to reach it.

Correcting current-gate documentation is this phase's core purpose, and tools/test_ci.py only pins the gate number in the workflow (lines 82 and 341), not in docs/RELEASE.md.

findings.description: When a published file has been deleted from the working tree, `current.read_bytes()` raises FileNotFoundError (an OSError), not the ValueError that every other rejection path uses. The CLI wrapper at line 93 catches OSError so the command still fails closed, but tools/test_g10_release.py:37 only exercises change, addition, symlink, malformed-receipt and unsafe-path cases against `payload.verify`, so deletion of a published SDK input is untested at the function boundary and any future caller that catches only ValueError would silently miss it.
findings.required_fix: Raise ValueError ("Published SDK input is missing: " + name) when the file is absent or unreadable, and add a removal case to test_published_payload_check_rejects_source_drift_additions_and_unsafe_paths.

findings.description: The guard's trust anchor is the retained receipt's `files` rows, but nothing in this check ties that inventory back to `archiveSha256`, and docs/checks/ is excluded from the review fingerprint (tools/review_phase.py:13), so the receipt is not itself hashed into source_sha256. A coordinated edit of a receipt row plus the matching working-tree file would pass this check. In practice it is caught elsewhere — tools/test_ci.py:264 pins archiveSha256/sourceCommit/date against CHANGELOG.md (which is hashed), and tools/live_evidence.py --check re-derives runtime_fingerprint for the whole src/examples tree via the digest pinned in contracts/live-evidence.json — but the new guard alone does not establish the receipt's integrity.
